response: Kell alloimmunization in pregnancy is not typically associated with fetal thrombocytopenia. In fact, studies have shown that fetuses with severe anemia due to Kell alloimmunization are generally not at risk for substantial thrombocytopenia, unlike those with severe anemia due to RhD alloimmunization. This suggests that Kell alloimmunization primarily affects fetal red blood cells, rather than platelets.
